result.topic_en: Euler sets up eight boundary and junction conditions (vanishing displacement and matching slope and curvature at an intermediate support L, plus conditions at the two ends E and F) for the eight coefficients of the vibrating elastic rod's two segments, and begins solving them.
result.transcription:
) 152 (
portio in L cum axe facit, neceſſario aequales eſſe debent; neque vero etiam radius oſculi in hoc puncto L vtrinque diuerſus eſſe poteſt. His obſeruatis pro hoc puncto L, vbi fit $u=\lambda$, quia vtraque applicata $y$ euaneſcere debet, habebimus ſequentes quatuor aequationes:
$\text{I. } \alpha e^{\lambda\omega}+\beta e^{-\lambda\omega}+\gamma\,\text{ſin.}\,\lambda\omega+\delta\,\text{coſ.}\,\lambda\omega=0.$
$\text{II. } \alpha' e^{\lambda\omega}+\beta' e^{-\lambda\omega}+\gamma'\,\text{ſin.}\,\lambda\omega=\delta'\,\text{coſ.}\,\lambda\omega=0.$
$\text{III. } \alpha e^{\lambda\omega}-\beta e^{-\lambda\omega}+\gamma\,\text{coſ.}\,\lambda\omega-\delta\,\text{ſin.}\,\lambda\omega$
$=\alpha' e^{\lambda\omega}-\beta' e^{-\lambda\omega}+\gamma'\,\text{coſ.}\,\lambda\omega-\delta'\,\text{ſin.}\,\lambda\omega.$ ſiue
$\text{III. } (\alpha-\alpha')e^{\lambda\omega}-(\beta-\beta')e^{-\lambda\omega}+(\gamma-\gamma')\,\text{coſ.}\,\lambda\omega$
$-(\delta-\delta')\,\text{ſin.}\,\lambda\omega=0.$
$\text{IV. } (\alpha-\alpha')e^{\lambda\omega}+(\beta-\beta')e^{-\lambda\omega}-(\gamma-\gamma')\,\text{ſin.}\,\lambda\omega$
$-(\delta-\delta')\,\text{coſ.}\,\lambda\omega=0.$
Nunc igitur ad vtrumque quoque terminum ſpectemus, vnde etiam quatuor reſultabunt aequationes, prouti fuerit vel $\lambda=0$ vel $\lambda=1$; terminus ſcilicet E, vbi $u=0$, praebet:
$\text{V. } \alpha+\beta+\delta=0$ et $\text{VI. } \alpha+\beta-\delta=0,$
terminus autem F, vbi $u=1$, dat
$\text{VII. } \alpha' e^{\omega}+\beta' e^{-\omega}+\gamma'\,\text{ſin.}\,\omega+\delta'\,\text{coſ.}\,\omega=0$ et
$\text{VIII. } \alpha' e^{\omega}+\beta' e^{-\omega}-\gamma'\,\text{ſin.}\,\omega-\delta'\,\text{coſ.}\,\omega=0.$
Nacti ſcilicet ſumus octo aequationes pro definiendis octo coëfficientibus, $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$, $\delta$ et $\alpha'$, $\beta'$, $\gamma'$, $\delta'$; ac tum ſupererit adhuc aequatio, vnde angulum $\omega$ definiri apportebit. Incipiamus ab aequatione V et VI, ex quibus ſtatim colligitur $\beta=-\alpha$ et $\delta=0$; deinde VII et VIII, inuicem additae dant $\alpha' e^{\omega}+\beta' e^{-\omega}=0$, ſubtractae vero dant
$\gamma'$ ſin.

items.quote: Nacti ſcilicet ſumus octo aequationes pro definiendis octo coëfficientibus, $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$, $\delta$ et $\alpha'$, $\beta'$, $\gamma'$, $\delta'$; ac tum ſupererit adhuc aequatio, vnde angulum $\omega$ definiri apportebit.
items.english: We have thus obtained eight equations for determining the eight coefficients α, β, γ, δ and α', β', γ', δ'; and then there will still remain an equation from which the angle ω must be determined.

items.quote: Incipiamus ab aequatione V et VI, ex quibus ſtatim colligitur $\beta=-\alpha$ et $\delta=0$
items.english: Let us begin with equations V and VI, from which it is immediately concluded that β = −α and δ = 0.

items.quote: deinde VII et VIII, inuicem additae dant $\alpha' e^{\omega}+\beta' e^{-\omega}=0$
items.english: Then VII and VIII, added together, give α'e^ω + β'e^{−ω} = 0.
